decisions.id: B5-no-pair
decisions.summary: Bookends row 5: no timing pair at batch 5's (wave 106's) close because its engine code is off the pair's path
decisions.why: Carried from wave 107's round 1; HEAD~1 changes plan.md only in the Wave 107 bullet. Narrows FR-003's literal 'one timing pair and its perf-audit', exactly as B4-no-pair did, and B4's stated condition (holds only while a batch's engine code stays off the hamlet roll path) is re-measured here, not carried over. The batch's engine delta (git diff de5f96acb..HEAD on l7r/pool): compound_model.py, compound_parts.py, pack_audit (__init__, checks, registry), buildings/types.json (the tubs_off_their_doors check name added to two types' check lists), and four modal .md files; no pool gen or pool json. Measured: importing exactly what perf_snapshot imports (hamletgen, hamletgen.driver, hamletgen.plan, settlement, _invocation, tools.perf_bands) loads 247 l7r modules, none of compound, compound_model, compound_parts, pack_audit or buildings.*; the one name-alike, settlement.structures.compounds, imports only _geom and _knobs; no file under hamletgen/ or settlement/ reads types.json, DOOR_KINDS or TUB_DOOR_MAX_FT; _invocation names compound and pack_audit only as strings in a table. So the pair would time byte-identical code and could detect nothing this batch did - the rule's purpose cannot be served, and a band-3 noise reading would send the GM a sign-off on nothing. The gate premise also checks: .git/verification-state.json records make done green-local at 7817f4a30, engine key 4ade95493877..., the current key, and HEAD changes no engine path after it. Residue (not a ruling): the row's list of the batch's engine code omits buildings/types.json, which batch 4's row named; add it so the row states the whole delta it rests on.
